To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) halophytes can be used as a source of genes and traits to improve salinity tolerance in non halophyte species; 2) trichome shape and size, stomatal density, and xylem ion transport are key traits that need to be targeted for improvement of salt tolerance in crops.

halophytes have evolved a range of physiological strategies that could be exploited to enhance salinity tolerance in non-halophyte crop species, and that the most important of these are trichome-based Na( sequestrations, efficient control of xleym ion loading, stomata aperture control, and vacuolar Na( sequestraion.

the physiological traits that need to be introduced into traditional crop plants in order to improve their salinity tolerance include: (1) the ability to control xylem ion load, (2) the ability to maintain K( homeostasis and Na( sequestation in the vacuole, (3) the ability to regulate stomata aperture to optimize water use efficiency, and (4) the ability to sequester Na( outside the plant body.

understanding the genetic and physiological bases of salinity tolerance and the development of strategies for the improvement of crop salinity tolerance by the introduction of halophytic traits and genes into non halophytes.
